podcast.title: Decca's Interest in Signing Her
podcast.body: Bob Thiel at Decca Records was persuaded to sign Jackie Wilson partly because Wilson's manager, Al Green, promised he could also sign LaVern Baker when her contract with Atlantic expired. "But because Green promised that he could also sign Le Verne Baker, when her contract with Atlantic expired."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-Four: "Reet Petite" by Jackie Wilson

podcast.title: Performer at Alan Freed Show
podcast.body: LaVern Baker was one of the R&B stars Carole King saw perform at an Alan Freed show at the Paramount in Brooklyn, which was a pivotal experience for King in deciding her career path. "Zwick took her to an Alan Fried show at the Paramount in Brooklyn, where she saw Le Verne Baker, BB King, Mickey Baker, The Moon Glows, and several other R&B stars of the period."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.title: Recorded with Atlantic Session Musicians
podcast.body: LaVern Baker was an artist who recorded using the standard Atlantic session musicians and arrangers, the same ensemble that backed Ray Charles on his records during that period. "The same people who were making records with Ruth Brown or LeVern Baker."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 32: "I Got A Woman" by Ray Charles

podcast.title: String of R&B Hits
podcast.body: LaVern Baker had achieved a string of R&B hits by the time Al Green (mobster) managed her. "And also LeVern Baker, who had had a string of Arvind B hits."
